Nearly all UK employees below director level are eligible to vote. If successful, the union would become the largest recognized union in the UK games industry, giving workers a collective voice. The proposed recognition agreement follows four months of negotiations between Rockstar management and employees. It would allow workers to negotiate over pay, overtime, pensions, bonuses, leave and other employment conditions, while securing consultation rights over HR policies and AI. The vote comes at a particularly busy time for Rockstar, with GTA VI finally due to arrive on November 19, more than 13 years after its predecessor. The game is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history, although the people responsible for making it have rather more immediate concerns than sales records. events.excerpt: "Train in Python, serve in C++" might as well be Google's motto when it comes to much of its ML work. Python is easy for data scientists to wield, but keeping its interpreter in the serving pipeline can add overhead and deployment headaches. The industry-backed OpenXLA Project provides tools for compiling machine learning computations into native code for different processors. The latest component of this setup to be open sourced is XSE , short for the XLA Serving Engine. One-shot inference XSE is not so much suited for large-scale LLM inference (which would be better served by vLLM or SGLang ), but rather for smaller, more sharply task-oriented models, of which there are plenty at Google. "LLM serving gets most of the attention right now, but a significant amount of production inference is still ranking, recommendation, embedding, and vision models. These tend to be short requests with very high [queries-per-second] and tight latency budgets," Nathan Beach , Google director of product management, wrote in a LinkedIn missive Tuesday. At Google, XSE already handles more than six million queries per second across services including YouTube Shorts, Google Ads, and Search. These models aren't there for a leisurely chat. They rank results, recommend videos, and make other decisions on the fly, often without users noticing. A Python interpreter mulling each request would be a bottleneck, if not the end of Google itself. In Google's tests on short requests, XSE delivered two to five times the throughput of its best optimized Python server, using a quarter of the memory. No Python

events.excerpt: Daniil Ankushin, Nethermind. Verify-budget figures: method by Daniil Ankushin, benchmark and measurements by Manuel Arto. On frame transactions a shielded pool pays its own gas, so a private withdrawal needs no relayer. We ran a real BN254 Groth16 pool this way on current Nethermind master: a withdrawal costs 679,322 gas. With EIP-8250 nonce keys, many withdrawals can come from the one pool address at once. Two things do not work yet. The proof check is over the spec cap on validation gas, and a pool cannot pay for a call from the user’s own address. The pool we ran is soispoke’s minimal-shielded-pool ( GitHub - soispoke/minimal-shielded-pool · GitHub ). How a withdrawal works In a withdrawal the pool is the sender. Its VERIFY code checks the zk proof and approves execution and payment. The user needs no funded account and does not appear in the transaction. Two drafts make this safe in a public mempool. With EIP-8250 the pool uses the note’s nullifiers as nonce keys. Each withdrawal has its own nonce key, so withdrawals with the pool as sender do not compete for one nonce. A side effect: a nullifier that was already used is a used nonce key, so the protocol refuses a double spend before the pool’s code runs. With EIP-8272 the transaction checks the pool’s Merkle root against a contract of recent roots before the pool’s code runs, so a mempool node never reads the pool’s storage. What it costs All values are from mined receipts on Nethermind master 4bcb9e30, single node. Step Gas Deposit a note, frame tx 990,503 of which state gas 195,840 Deposit a note, plain EIP-1559 call
